author: cli
text: Does NOT extract doc comments. GoParser and JavaScriptParser both carry a leading_doc() that lifts documentation above a declaration into RawEntity.doc; JavaParser omits it, so Javadoc never reaches the map and Java entities are the only ones whose comment-rot detection has nothing to compare.

author: cli
text: Does NOT extract method signatures - RawEntity is built without the signature argument, leaving an empty string. Go and JS/TS both emit name(params) result, so before_edit can state a contract for every language except Java.

author: cli
text: Does NOT extract field declarations as entities: walk() handles class_declaration and method_declaration but not field_declaration, so fields stay in body_text untracked. PythonParser DOES extract class attributes, so the two disagree. Unproven hunch: an oversight rather than a deliberate choice, given the Python precedent.

author: cli
text: Re-read at 0.56.0. The overload-disambiguation reasoning below still holds exactly - always-suffix rather than suffix-only-when-needed, because the two-pass alternative would make identity depend on how many overloads happen to exist today. What changed is that the suffix is no longer built here by hand: refs.render produces it, and the same producer spells the CALL reference from the argument count at the invocation. That is what turned 0 method-level call edges into 3150 on gson.

author: cli
text: Re-read at 0.57.2. The three limitations recorded below are unchanged and still true. The call emission now also carries via_attr and bare, taken from whether method_invocation has an `object` field. Java's builtin_names is empty, so the builtin rule never fires here; the fields are recorded because the attribute-call rule reads via_attr and because a parser that answers 'unknown' would make every future rule guess.

author: cli
text: Re-read at the literal-receiver change. Comments verified and unchanged; the emission gained literal_recv. builtin_names stays empty - correct, and unrelated to this rule.
